# About ##### Last updated August 17th 2026 STARLING (con**ST**ruction of intrinsic**A**lly diso**R**dered proteins ensembles efficient**L**y v**I**a multi-dime**N**sional **G**enerative models) is a latent-space probabilistic denoising diffusion model for predicting coarse-grained ensembles of intrinsically disordered regions. STARLING was developed by **Borna Novak** and **Jeff Lotthammer** in the [Holehouse lab](https://www.holehouselab.com/) (with some occasional help from Ryan and Alex, as is their wont). For more information, please take a look at our paper! Novak, B., Lotthammer, J. M., Emenecker, R. J. & Holehouse, A. S. [**Accurate predictions of disordered protein ensembles with STARLING.** ](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10141-2) *Nature* **652,** 240–250 (2026). # Documentation Detailed documentation is provdied on readthedocs, although this readme is probably enough to do most things. [https://idptools-starling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/](https://idptools-starling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) # Colab notebook A Google Colab notebook for predicting ensembles and performing rudimentary analysis [is available here](https://colab.research.google.com/github/idptools/idpcolab/blob/main/STARLING/STARLING_demo.ipynb). --- # Installation STARLING is available on GitHub (bleeding edge) and on PyPi (stable). We recommend creating a fresh conda environment for STARLING (although in principle, there's nothing special about the STARLING environment) ```bash conda create -n starling python=3.11 -y conda activate starling ``` You can then install STARLING from PyPI using pip (or uv): ```bash pip install idptools-starling ``` Or you can install the bleeding-edge version from GitHub: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/idptools/starling.git ``` To check that STARLING has been installed correctly, run starling --help A Docker image is also available — see the [Docker documentation](docker/readme.md) for details. --- # Quickstart The easiest way to use STARLING for ensemble generation is with the `starling` command-line tool. starling -c 400 --outname my_cool_idr -r Example: starling MDVFMKGLSKAKEGVVAAAEKTKQGVAEAAGKTKEGVLYVGSKTKEGVVHGVATVAEKTKEQVTNVGGAVVTGVTAVAQKTVEGAGSIAAATGFVKKDQLGKNEEGAPQEGILEDMPVDPDNEAYEMPSEEGYQDYEPEA --outname synuclein -r Will generate three files: * `synuclein.starling` — the full STARLING ensemble file. This holds all the information associated with the ensemble. * `synuclein_STARLING.pdb` — the topology file for the ensemble. * `synuclein_STARLING.xtc` — the trajectory file for the ensemble. By default, STARLING generates 400 conformations — to change the number of conformations, use the `-c` flag (e.g., `-c 1000` would generate an ensemble with 1000 conformations). # Performance STARLING is VERY fast on GPUs and — honestly — VERY fast on Apple Silicon as well. It is a bit slower on CPUs, but we're talking minutes instead of seconds for ensemble generation. --- # Command-Line Interface (CLI) STARLING installs several command-line tools. Below is a complete reference for all of them. ## `starling` — Ensemble Generation The main CLI tool. Generates conformational ensembles from amino acid sequences. ```bash starling [options] ``` **Input formats:** a raw amino acid sequence, a `.fasta` file, a `.tsv` file (`namesequence`), or a `.seq.in` file. **Examples:** ```bash # Single sequence, 400 conformations with 3D structures starling MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY -c 400 -r --outname my_protein # From a FASTA file, using GPU starling proteins.fasta -c 200 -d cuda:0 -r -o ./results # Print STARLING configuration info starling --info ``` ### Options | Flag | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `user_input` | positional | — | Sequence string, FASTA file, TSV file, or `.seq.in` file | | `-c, --conformations` | int | 400 | Number of conformations to generate | | `--steps` | int | 30 | Number of DDIM denoising steps | | `-d, --device` | str | auto | Device: `cpu`, `cuda:0`, `cuda:1`, `mps`, etc. | | `-b, --batch_size` | int | 100 | Batch size for sampling | | `-o, --output_directory` | str | `.` | Output directory for saving results | | `--outname` | str | auto | Override output filename prefix (single sequence only) | | `-r, --return_structures` | flag | off | Generate PDB + XTC 3D structures | | `--ionic_strength` | int | 150 | Solvent ionic strength in mM (20, 150, or 300) | | `--remove-errors` | flag | off | Discard physically impossible conformations and regenerate replacements, so the output still contains `-c` conformations | | `-v, --verbose` | flag | off | Enable verbose output | | `--disable_progress_bar` | flag | off | Hide progress bars | | `--info` | flag | — | Print STARLING configuration and exit | | `--version` | flag | — | Print version and exit | ### Output files | File | Description | |------|-------------| | `*.starling` | Binary ensemble archive (distance maps + metadata) | | `*_STARLING.pdb` | PDB topology (when `-r` is used) | | `*_STARLING.xtc` | XTC trajectory with all conformations (when `-r` is used) | --- ## `starling-benchmark` — Performance Benchmarking Profile model throughput and measure performance across different configurations. ```bash starling-benchmark [options] ``` **Examples:** ```bash # Default benchmark sweep (10 to 1000 conformations) starling-benchmark --device cuda:0 # Single run with 500 conformations and model compilation starling-benchmark --device cuda:0 --single-run 500 --compile ``` ### Options | Flag | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `--device` | str | auto | Device for benchmarking | | `--batch-size` | int | 100 | Batch size | | `--steps` | int | 30 | Diffusion steps | | `--sequence` | str | alpha-synuclein | Test sequence (default: 140 aa) | | `--cooltime` | int | 20 | Cooldown seconds between runs | | `--single-run` | int | 0 | Single test with N conformations (0 = sweep series) | | `--compile` | flag | off | Enable PyTorch model compilation (CUDA only) | --- ## File Conversion Tools STARLING ships with several converters for working with `.starling` ensemble archives. ### `starling2pdb` — Convert to PDB ```bash starling2pdb my_ensemble.starling -o ./output ``` Generates a multi-model PDB trajectory file. ### `starling2xtc` — Convert to XTC ```bash starling2xtc my_ensemble.starling -o ./output ``` Generates a PDB topology file plus a compressed XTC trajectory file. ### `starling2numpy` — Convert to NumPy ```bash starling2numpy my_ensemble.starling -o ./output ``` Exports the raw distance maps as a NumPy `.npy` array with shape `(n_conformations, n_residues, n_residues)`. ### `starling2sequence` — Print sequence ```bash starling2sequence my_ensemble.starling ``` Prints the amino acid sequence stored in the `.starling` archive to stdout. ### `starling2info` — Print ensemble metadata ```bash starling2info my_ensemble.starling ``` Displays metadata about the ensemble, including creation date, sequence, number of conformations, radius of gyration, end-to-end distance, and model weights used. ### `starling2starling` — Repair/validate an archive ```bash # Check for errors starling2starling my_ensemble.starling --error-check # Check and remove problematic conformations starling2starling my_ensemble.starling --error-check --remove-errors -o fixed_ # Overwrite the original file starling2starling my_ensemble.starling --error-check --remove-errors --overwrite ``` ### `numpy2starling` — Restore from NumPy ```bash numpy2starling distance_maps.npy -s MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY -o ./output ``` Converts a NumPy distance map array and a sequence back into a `.starling` archive. Supports optional `--build-structures` to reconstruct 3D coordinates, and `-x` / `-p` to attach existing XTC/PDB trajectories. ### `xtc2starling` — Convert XTC trajectory to STARLING ```bash xtc2starling --xtc trajectory.xtc --pdb topology.pdb -o ./output ``` Converts an existing XTC trajectory and PDB topology into a `.starling` archive. ### Converter summary | Command | Input | Output | Description | |---------|-------|--------|-------------| | `starling2pdb` | `.starling` | `.pdb` | Multi-model PDB trajectory | | `starling2xtc` | `.starling` | `.pdb` + `.xtc` | Topology + compressed trajectory | | `starling2numpy` | `.starling` | `.npy` | Raw distance maps as NumPy array | | `starling2sequence` | `.starling` | stdout | Print amino-acid sequence | | `starling2info` | `.starling` | stdout | Print metadata (version, date, Rg, etc.) | | `starling2starling` | `.starling` | `.starling` | Re-save with optional error removal | | `numpy2starling` | `.npy` | `.starling` | Restore archive from NumPy | | `xtc2starling` | `.xtc` + `.pdb` | `.starling` | Convert MD trajectory to STARLING | --- ## `starling-search` — Sequence Search STARLING includes a FAISS-based similarity search engine that uses ensemble-aware sequence embeddings. It has two subcommands: `build` and `query`. ### `starling-search query` — Find similar sequences Search the pre-built FAISS index for sequences with similar ensemble properties. ```bash starling-search query \ --seq MDVFMKGLSKAKEGVVAAAEKTKQGVAEAAGKT \ --k 20 \ --nprobe 128 \ --exclude-exact \ --out search_results ``` ```bash # With filtering by sequence identity and length starling-search query \ --seq MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY \ --k 50 \ --sequence-identity-max 0.9 \ --length-min 40 \ --length-max 800 \ --rerank \ --out-format csv \ --out filtered_results ``` #### Query options | Flag | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `--index` | str | `default` | FAISS index path; `default` auto-downloads the pre-built index | | `--seq` | str | — | Query sequence(s), can be specified multiple times | | `--k` | int | 10 | Number of nearest neighbors to return | | `--nprobe` | int | 64 | FAISS probe count (higher = slower but more accurate) | | `--metric` | str | `cosine` | Distance metric: `cosine` or `l2` | | `--exclude-exact` | flag | on | Skip exact sequence matches in results | | `--sequence-identity-max` | float | — | Maximum sequence identity threshold | | `--identity-denominator` | str | `query` | How to compute identity: `query`, `target`, `max`, `min`, `avg` | | `--length-min` | int | — | Minimum target sequence length | | `--length-max` | int | — | Maximum target sequence length | | `--max-cosine-similarity` | float | — | Pre-filter upper bound on cosine similarity | | `--min-l2-distance` | float | — | Pre-filter lower bound on L2 distance | | `--rerank` | flag | on | Re-embed top hits with full encoder for more accurate ranking | | `--rerank-batch-size` | int | 64 | Batch size for reranking | | `--rerank-device` | str | auto | Device for reranking | | `--rerank-ionic-strength` | int | auto | Ionic strength for reranking | | `--device` | str | `cuda:0` | Device for query embedding | | `--batch-size` | int | 256 | Batch size for embedding | | `--ionic-strength` | int | 150 | Ionic strength in mM for encoding | | `-o, --out` | str | `nearest_neighbors` | Output file basename | | `--out-format` | str | `csv` | Output format: `csv` or `jsonl` | | `--verbose` | flag | on | Verbose logging | ### `starling-search build` — Build a custom FAISS index Build a FAISS index from pre-tokenized sequences (advanced usage). ```bash starling-search build \ --root /data/corpus \ --tokens /data/corpus/tokens \ --index /indexes/my_index.faiss \ --sample-size 1000000 \ --nlist 32768 \ --use-gpu ``` #### Build options | Flag | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `--root` | str | required | Root data directory | | `--index` | str | required | Output FAISS index path | | `--tokens` | str | required | Directory with pre-tokenized sequences | | `--metric` | str | `cosine` | Distance metric: `cosine` or `l2` | | `--sample-size` | int | 655360 | Training sample size | | `--nlist` | int | 16384 | FAISS IVF nlist parameter | | `--m` | int | 64 | HNSW M parameter | | `--nbits` | int | 8 | Quantization bits | | `--add-batch-size` | int | 100000 | Batch size for adding vectors | | `--nprobe` | int | 16 | FAISS probe count | | `--use-gpu` | flag | on | Use GPU for index building | | `--gpu-device` | int | 0 | GPU device ID | | `--gpu-fp16-lut` | flag | on | Use FP16 lookup tables on GPU | | `--opq` | flag | off | Enable Optimized Product Quantization | | `--compress` | flag | off | Compress sequences | | `--shard-regex` | str | — | Regex filter for shard files | | `--verbose` | flag | on | Verbose output | --- ## `starling-pretokenize` — Pre-tokenize Sequences Pre-encode FASTA files for rapid FAISS index construction (used before `starling-search build`). ```bash starling-pretokenize sequences/*.fasta \ --output tokens_dir \ --combined \ --workers 4 ``` ### Options | Flag | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `fastas` | positional | — | Input FASTA file(s) | | `-o, --output` | str | required | Output directory for token files | | `--combined` | flag | off | Merge all into a single `.pt` file | | `--prefix` | str | `pretokenized` | Prefix for combined output file | | `--sequences` | str | — | Text file with FASTA paths (one per line) | | `--workers` | int | 1 | Number of parallel tokenizer workers | | `--no-progress` | flag | off | Hide progress bars | --- ## Training CLIs (Advanced) These tools are primarily used for model development and retraining. | Command | Description | |---------|-------------| | `starling-vae-train` | Train the VAE encoder model | | `starling-ddpm-train` | Train the diffusion model | These commands depend on Hydra, OmegaConf and Weights & Biases, which are **not** part of the default install because they are not needed to generate ensembles. To use them, install STARLING with the `train` extra. From PyPI: ```bash pip install "idptools-starling[train]" ``` Straight from GitHub, without cloning — note that the extra attaches to the *package name*, not to the URL: ```bash pip install "idptools-starling[train] @ git+https://github.com/idptools/starling.git" ``` To pin a branch, tag or commit, append it to the URL with `@`: ```bash pip install "idptools-starling[train] @ git+https://github.com/idptools/starling.git@main" ``` From a local clone: ```bash pip install ".[train]" # or, for an editable development install pip install -e ".[train]" ``` > **Keep the quotes.** In `zsh` (the default shell on macOS) an unquoted `pip install idptools-starling[train]` is treated as a glob and fails with `zsh: no matches found`. Quoting works in every shell. --- # Python Library As well as the command-line tools, STARLING provides a powerful Python API for generating and analyzing ensembles programmatically. ## Supported input formats All main API functions accept sequences in multiple formats: | Format | Example | |--------|---------| | Single sequence string | `'MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY'` | | List of sequences | `['MKVIFLA...', 'MDVFMKG...']` | | Dictionary of name→sequence | `{'protein_a': 'MKVIFLA...', 'protein_b': 'MDVFMKG...'}` | | Path to a `.fasta` file | `'proteins.fasta'` | | Path to a `.tsv` / `.seq.in` file | `'sequences.tsv'` (tab-separated `name\tsequence`) | --- ## `generate()` — Generate Ensembles The `generate` function is the main entry point for generating conformational ensembles using the STARLING model. It accepts various input types, generates conformations using DDIM/DDPM, and optionally returns 3D structures. ```python from starling import generate ``` ### Basic usage ```python # Single sequence → single Ensemble object E = generate('MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY', return_single_ensemble=True) # List of sequences → dict of Ensemble objects E_dict = generate(['MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY', 'MDVFMKGLSKAKEGVVAAAEKTKQGVAE']) # Dictionary of sequences → dict of Ensemble objects E_dict = generate({'seq1': 'MKVIFLAVLGLGIVVTTVLY', 'seq2': 'MDVFMKGLSKAKEGVVAAAEKTKQGVAE'}) # From a FASTA file, with 3D structures, saved to disk E_dict = generate('proteins.fasta', conformations=500, return_structures=True, output_directory='./results') ``` ### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |-----------|------|---------|-------------| | `user_input` | str / list / dict | — | Input sequences (see supported formats above) | | `conformations` | int | 400 | Number of conformations to generate | | `ionic_strength` | int | 150 | Solvent ionic strength in mM (20, 150, or 300) | | `device` | str | `None` (auto) | Device: `'cpu'`, `'cuda:0'`, `'mps'`, etc. | | `steps` | int | 30 | Number of denoising steps | | `sampler` | str | `'ddim'` | Sampler backend | | `return_structures` | bool | `False` | Generate 3D structures (PDB/XTC) | | `batch_size` | int | 100 | Batch size for sampling | | `output_directory` | str | `None` | Save directory (if set, writes `.starling` files to disk) | | `output_name` | str | `None` | Override filename prefix (single-sequence mode) | | `return_data` | bool | `True` | Return `Ensemble` objects (set `False` for fire-and-forget disk saves) | | `verbose` | bool | `False` | Print status messages | | `show_progress_bar` | bool | `True` | Show global progress bar | | `show_per_step_progress_bar` | bool | `True` | Show per-step denoising progress bar | | `pdb_trajectory` | bool | `False` | Save PDB trajectory alongside XTC | | `return_single_ensemble` | bool | `False` | Return a single `Ensemble` instead of a dict (single-sequence mode) | | `constraint` | Constraint | `None` | Constraint object for guided generation | | `encoder_path` | str | `None` | Custom encoder model checkpoint | | `ddpm_path` | str | `None` | Custom diffusion model checkpoint | ### Returns - **`dict[str, Ensemble]`** — by default (one entry per input sequence) - **`Ensemble`** — when `return_single_ensemble=True` and a single sequence is provided - **`None`** — when `return_data=False` --- ## `sequence_encoder()` — Ensemble-Aware Sequence Embeddings STARLING jointly trains a transformer-based sequence encoder that produces embeddings optimized for ensemble generation. Sequences with similar ensemble properties tend to have similar embeddings, making them useful for search and design applications. ```python from starling import sequence_encoder ``` ### Basic usage ```python # Residue-level embeddings (returns dict of name → tensor with shape (L, D)) embeddings = sequence_encoder('proteins.fasta') # Protein-level embeddings via mean pooling embeddings = sequence_encoder('proteins.fasta', aggregate=True) # With custom settings embeddings = sequence_encoder( {'prot_a': 'MKVIFLA...', 'prot_b': 'MDVFMKG...'}, ionic_strength=150, batch_size=64, aggregate=True, device='cuda:0', ) ``` ### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |-----------|------|---------|-------------| | `sequence_dict` | str / list / dict | — | Input sequences (same formats as `generate()`) | | `ionic_strength` | int | 150 | Ionic strength in mM | | `batch_size` | int | 32 | Sequences per batch | | `aggregate` | bool | `False` | Return protein-level (mean-pooled) embeddings instead of residue-level | | `device` | str | `None` (auto) | Target device | | `output_directory` | str | `None` | Optional directory to save embeddings | | `encoder_path` | str | `None` | Custom encoder checkpoint | | `ddpm_path` | str | `None` | Custom diffusion model checkpoint | | `pretokenized` | bool | `False` | Skip tokenization if inputs are already tokenized | | `bucket` | bool | `False` | Adaptive bucketing by sequence length (improves throughput for variable-length inputs) | | `bucket_size` | int | 32 | Max unique lengths per bucket | | `free_cuda_cache` | bool | `False` | Release CUDA memory after each batch | | `return_on_cpu` | bool | `True` | Move tensors to CPU before returning | ### Returns - **`dict[str, torch.Tensor]`** — keys are sequence names, values are tensors with shape `(L, D)` (residue-level) or `(D,)` (aggregated) --- ## `load_ensemble()` — Load a Saved Ensemble Reload a previously generated and saved STARLING ensemble from disk. ```python from starling import load_ensemble ensemble = load_ensemble('path/to/my_favorite_ensemble.starling') # Load without 3D structures (faster) ensemble = load_ensemble('my_ensemble.starling', ignore_structures=True) ``` ### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |-----------|------|---------|-------------| | `filename` | str | — | Path to a `.starling` file | | `ignore_structures` | bool | `False` | Skip loading 3D structures for faster loading | ### Returns - **`Ensemble`** object --- ## `set_compilation_options()` — PyTorch Model Compilation If you intend to use STARLING repeatedly (e.g., in loops or batch processing), enable `torch.compile` to optimize model kernels. This adds overhead during the first call but improves subsequent runs by approximately 40% (tested on NVIDIA A5000). ```python import starling # Enable compilation starling.set_compilation_options(enabled=True) # Enable with custom options starling.set_compilation_options( enabled=True, mode='max-autotune', backend='inductor', fullgraph=True, ) ``` ### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |-----------|------|---------|-------------| | `enabled` | bool | `None` | Enable or disable compilation | | `mode` | str | `'default'` | Compilation mode: `'default'`, `'reduce-overhead'`, `'max-autotune'` | | `backend` | str | `'inductor'` | Compilation backend | | `fullgraph` | bool | `True` | Compile full graph | | `dynamic` | bool | `None` | Handle dynamic shapes | ### Returns - **`dict`** with the current compilation settings --- ## `Ensemble` Class The `Ensemble` class represents an ensemble of conformations for a protein chain. It stores distance maps from which all structural parameters can be derived. ### Properties | Property | Type | Description | |----------|------|-------------| | `.sequence` | str | Amino acid sequence | | `.number_of_conformations` | int | Total number of conformations | | `.sequence_length` | int | Number of residues | | `.has_structures` | bool | Whether 3D structures are available | | `.trajectory` | SSProtein | 3D trajectory object (lazy-built on first access) | ### Structural analysis methods #### `.rij()` — Inter-residue distance ```python Ensemble.rij(i, j, return_mean=False, use_bme_weights=False) ``` Returns the distance between residues `i` and `j` across all conformations, or the mean distance if `return_mean=True`. #### `.end_to_end_distance()` — End-to-end distance ```python Ensemble.end_to_end_distance(return_mean=False, use_bme_weights=False) ``` Returns the end-to-end distance across all conformations, or the mean. #### `.radius_of_gyration()` — Radius of gyration ```python Ensemble.radius_of_gyration(return_mean=False, force_recompute=False, use_bme_weights=False) ``` Returns the radius of gyration across all conformations, or the mean. #### `.hydrodynamic_radius()` — Hydrodynamic radius ```python Ensemble.hydrodynamic_radius(return_mean=False, force_recompute=False, mode='nygaard', alpha1=0.216, alpha2=4.06, alpha3=0.821) ``` Computes the hydrodynamic radius from the ensemble. #### `.local_radius_of_gyration()` — Local Rg for a sub-region ```python Ensemble.local_radius_of_gyration(start, end, return_mean=False, use_bme_weights=False) ``` Returns the radius of gyration for a sub-region defined by residues `start` to `end`. #### `.distance_maps()` — Pairwise distance maps ```python Ensemble.distance_maps(return_mean=False, use_bme_weights=False) ``` Returns the raw distance maps as `(n, L, L)` NumPy arrays, or the average distance map if `return_mean=True`. #### `.contact_map()` — Contact maps ```python Ensemble.contact_map(contact_thresh=11, return_mean=False, return_summed=False) ``` Returns binary contact maps using a distance threshold. If `return_mean=True`, returns the contact probability (0–1) for each residue pair. If `return_summed=True`, returns summed contacts instead. ### 3D structure reconstruction #### `.build_ensemble_trajectory()` ```python Ensemble.build_ensemble_trajectory( batch_size=100, device=None, force_recompute=False, progress_bar=True, ) ``` Initializes 3D coordinates with classical MDS, then refines weighted distance stress using batched Torch SMACOF on CPU, CUDA, or MPS. Accurately predicted residue separations receive greater weight. Returns an `SSProtein` trajectory object. There are no random restarts or CPU-worker controls. ### Error checking #### `.check_for_errors()` ```python Ensemble.check_for_errors(remove_errors=False, verbose=True, rebuild_trajectory=False) ``` Scans for problematic conformations (e.g., impossible distances). Returns a list of bad frame indices. If `remove_errors=True`, removes them in place. ### Bayesian Maximum Entropy (BME) reweighting #### `.reweight_bme()` ```python Ensemble.reweight_bme(experimental_data, ensemble_properties, weights=None, verbose=True) ``` Performs BME reweighting against experimental data. After reweighting, structural property methods accept `use_bme_weights=True` for reweighted statistics. ### File I/O #### `.save()` — Save an ensemble to disk ```python Ensemble.save(filename_prefix, compress=False, reduce_precision=None, compression_algorithm='lzma', verbose=True) ``` Saves the ensemble as a `.starling` archive. #### `.save_trajectory()` — Save 3D trajectory ```python Ensemble.save_trajectory(filename_prefix, pdb_trajectory=False) ``` Saves the 3D trajectory as XTC (or PDB if `pdb_trajectory=True`). --- ## Constrained Generation STARLING allows you to generate structural ensembles with constraints — such as experimentally measured distances or local/global shape features. These are passed to `generate()` via the `constraint` parameter. ### Available constraint types ```python from starling.inference.constraints import ( DistanceConstraint, RgConstraint, ReConstraint, HelicityConstraint, BondConstraint, StericClashConstraint, MultiConstraint, ) ``` #### `DistanceConstraint` — target distance between two residues ```python constraint = DistanceConstraint(resid1=10, resid2=200, target=50) ``` #### `RgConstraint` — target radius of gyration ```python constraint = RgConstraint(target=50) ``` #### `ReConstraint` — target end-to-end distance ```python constraint = ReConstraint(target=100) ``` #### `HelicityConstraint` — enforce helical structure in a range ```python constraint = HelicityConstraint(resid_start=10, resid_end=100) ``` #### `BondConstraint` — maintain consecutive residue spacing ```python constraint = BondConstraint(bond_length=3.81) ``` #### `StericClashConstraint` — prevent steric clashes ```python constraint = StericClashConstraint(steric_clash_definition=5.0) ``` #### `MultiConstraint` — combine multiple constraints ```python constraint = MultiConstraint([ DistanceConstraint(resid1=10, resid2=200, target=50), RgConstraint(target=30), ]) ``` ### Applying constraints ```python ensemble = generate(sequence, constraint=constraint) ``` ### Tuning constraint parameters All constraints accept the following keyword arguments: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |-----------|------|---------|-------------| | `force_constant` | float | 2.0 | Strength of the constraint | | `tolerance` | float | 0.0 | Tolerance around the target value | | `schedule` | str | `'cosine'` | Weight schedule: `'cosine'` or `'bell_shaped'` | | `guidance_start` | float | 0.0 | When to start applying the constraint (0.0 = start of denoising) | | `guidance_end` | float | 1.0 | When to stop applying the constraint (1.0 = end of denoising) | **Guidance timing reference:** | Window | `guidance_start` | `guidance_end` | What's being denoised | |--------|-------------------|-----------------|----------------------| | Early | 0.0 | 0.3 | Mostly noise, minimal structural information | | Mid | 0.3 | 0.7 | Emerging structure, useful features begin to form | | Late | 0.7 | 1.0 | Fine details, near-final structural refinement | Experimenting with these parameters for your particular application is recommended. --- # FAQs/Help #### I get a NumPy compilation warning error!? Oh no! You get the following error message: A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in NumPy 2.2.3 as it may crash. To support both 1.x and 2.x versions of NumPy, modules must be compiled with NumPy 2.0. Some module may need to rebuild instead e.g. with 'pybind11>=2.12'. If you are a user of the module, the easiest solution will be to downgrade to 'numpy<2' or try to upgrade the affected module. We expect that some modules will need time to support NumPy 2. We have seen this if folks are trying to install on Intel Macs because (Py)Torch stopped supporting Intel Macs after torch=2.2.2. If you're NOT on an Intel mac, the recommended way to resolve us by upgrading torch: # recommended, but ANY version above 2.2.2 should work pip install torch==2.6.0 or if you're on an Intel mac and torch > 2.2.2 is not available, downgrade numpy: pip install numpy==1.26.1 #### Potential PyTorch / CUDA version issues If you are on an older version of CUDA, a torch version that *does not have the correct CUDA version* will be installed. This can cause a segfault when running STARLING. To fix this, you need to install torch for your specific CUDA version. For example, to install PyTorch on Linux using pip with a CUDA version of 12.1, you would run: ```bash pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121 ``` To figure out which version of CUDA you currently have (assuming you have a CUDA-enabled GPU that is set up correctly), you need to run: ```bash nvidia-smi ``` This should return information about your GPU, NVIDIA driver version, and your CUDA version at the top. Please see the [PyTorch install instructions](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) for more info. #### Maximum sequence length STARLING currently supports sequences up to **380 residues** in length. --- ## Copyright Copyright (c) 2024-2026, Borna Novak, Jeffrey Lotthammer, Alex Holehouse

one_liner: 该仓库是 Boltz-2 的 Colab 封装工具，提供生物分子结构预测与结合亲和力预测，虽非专门针对 IDP/IDR，但可迁移用于无序蛋白参与的分子互作建模。
card:
## 是什么

Boltz2-Notebook 是一个基于 Google Colab 的交互式前端，将 Boltz-2 扩散模型封装为引导式表单，用于生物分子（蛋白质、DNA、RNA 和小分子配体）的 3D 结构预测、结合亲和力估计和自包含报告生成。它无需安装、命令行或 YAML 编写，即可在浏览器中运行，同时支持在本地 Linux 机器上执行。

## 亮点

- **零配置交互**：通过引导式表单自动生成 Boltz-2 的 YAML 配置，无需手动编写参数文件。
- **多分子类型支持**：支持蛋白质、核酸、小分子配体（SMILES 或 CCD 代码）、修饰残基、环肽、共价键、口袋和接触约束。
- **结果可视化**：提供 3D 结构查看器、置信度分数（pLDDT、PAE、ipTM）和结合亲和力（IC50、pIC50、ΔG）的直观展示。
- **批量处理**：Batch 笔记本支持从 CSV 或 FASTA 文件输入多个任务，并自动排序。
- **错误诊断**：失败时提供原因和修复建议，并包含诊断工具 `python -m boltz2nb.doctor`。
- **跨版本兼容**：支持 Python 3.10-3.13，自动选择官方 Boltz 或社区 fork。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接服务于 IDR/IDP 与分子互作研究：
- **无序蛋白结构预测**：Boltz-2 的扩散模型可预测含无序区域的蛋白质结构，pLDDT 分数可识别低置信度（无序）区域。
- **结合亲和力预测**：对 IDR 介导的弱相互作用（如 LLPS 中的多价互作）提供 IC50 和 ΔG 估计，有助于筛选相分离驱动残基。
- **构象系综采样**：通过调整采样步数和扩散样本数，可生成多个构象，用于研究 IDP 的构象异质性。
- **可迁移的交互设计**：其引导式表单和结果可视化模式可复用于构建面向 IDP 研究者的友好工具。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：在 Colab 中打开 `Boltz2.ipynb`，选择 GPU 运行时（T4 或更好），依次运行单元格。
- **安装**：Cell 1 自动安装 `boltz2nb` 包和 Boltz 引擎（`boltz[cuda]==2.2.1` 或 `boltz-community[cuda]==2.10.12`），依赖见 `pyproject.toml`。
- **输入格式**：通过表单输入序列（FASTA 或直接粘贴）、配体 SMILES 或 CCD 代码，可上传自定义 MSA（`.a3m`）或模板（`.cif`/`.pdb`）。
- **输出**：结果保存在 `boltz_data/<job>/`，包括预测结构（PDB/mmCIF）、置信度分数、结合亲和力报告和 HTML 报告。
- **调试**：运行 `python -m boltz2nb.doctor /content/boltz_data/<job>` 检查输出一致性。
- **本地运行**：克隆仓库，`pip install -e ".[ligand,viewer]" "boltz[cuda]==2.2.1"`，然后运行 `scripts/common/Boltz_Run.py` 和 `scripts/common/analysis.py`。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学是将复杂的 Boltz-2 预测流程抽象为三个可组合的脚本（参数生成、运行、分析），通过表单驱动 YAML 构建，实现零门槛的扩散模型使用，同时保持结果的可解释性和可复现性。

## 可搬移点

- **`boltz2nb/yaml_builder.py`**：YAML 配置生成逻辑，可解耦用于自定义 Boltz-2 输入构建。
- **`boltz2nb/analysis.py`**：置信度映射和结合亲和力计算，可移植到其他结构预测管道。
- **`boltz2nb/run_params.py`**：运行参数序列化，便于自动化调参。
- **`boltz2nb/pdb_import.py`**：PDB/mmCIF 导入处理，可复用于 IDP 结构预处理。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改。

### Biomolecular structure and binding-affinity prediction with Boltz-2, in your browser [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/blob/main/Boltz2.ipynb) [![bioRxiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/bioRxiv-10.64898%2F2026.09.18.752645-b31b1b)](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.18.752645) [![CI](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-5A6985)](LICENSE) ![Python 3.10 to 3.13](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10%E2%80%933.13-3B4FD6?logo=python&logoColor=white) [Website](https://atharvatilewale.github.io/boltz2-notebook/) · [Guide](https://atharvatilewale.github.io/boltz2-notebook/docs/use-cases.html) · [FAQ](https://atharvatilewale.github.io/boltz2-notebook/docs/faq.html) · [Paper](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.18.752645) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/issues)
--- **Boltz2-Notebook** puts [Boltz-2](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz) behind a guided form in Google Colab. Describe your molecules (proteins, DNA, RNA and small-molecule ligands), press run, and get a predicted 3-D structure with confidence scores, a binding-affinity estimate and a self-contained report. No installation, no command line, no YAML to write. The same code also runs on your own Linux machine. ## Quick start 1. **Open the [default notebook in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/blob/main/Boltz2.ipynb)** and choose *Runtime ▸ Change runtime type ▸ T4 GPU*. 2. Run **Install** and **Download model weights**, once per session (about 6 GB of model files). 3. Run **Generate Parameters**, describe your system in the form and press **Save configuration**. 4. Run **Run Boltz2 Engine** (2 to 10 minutes on a T4), then **Analyse Results** for the plots, the 3-D viewer and the HTML report. ## Choose a notebook | Notebook | Use it for | Status | | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | **Advanced** (default) | Everything: proteins, DNA/RNA, ligands, templates, constraints, covalent bonds, modified residues, custom MSA | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/Stable-Default-green) | [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/blob/main/Boltz2.ipynb) | | **Standard** | Proteins and small-molecule ligands, with a shorter form | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/Stable-Mature-green) | [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/blob/main/colab/v1/Boltz2_v1.0.0.ipynb) | | **Batch** | Screening many inputs from a CSV or FASTA file, with ranking | ![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pre--release-Experimental-orange) | [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/blob/main/batch/Boltz2_Batch_v1_beta.ipynb) | Not sure? Start with **Advanced**: it does everything the Standard notebook does. The Batch notebook has its own [guide](batch/README.md).
Feature comparison | Feature | Advanced | Standard | Batch | |:--|:--:|:--:|:--:| | Proteins and multi-chain complexes | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Small-molecule ligands (SMILES or CCD code) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Binding affinity | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | DNA and RNA | ✅ | – | ✅ | | Uploaded MSA (`.a3m`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Structural templates | ✅ | – | ✅ | | Covalent bonds, pocket and contact constraints | ✅ | – | – | | Modified residues, cyclic peptides | ✅ | – | – | | Import chains and ligands from a PDB or mmCIF file | ✅ | ✅ | – | | Many jobs from a CSV or FASTA file, with ranking | – | – | ✅ | | 3-D viewer and HTML report per job | ✅ | ✅ | summary table |
## What you get | Input builder | Live run panel | |:--|:--| | ![Input builder with a protein, a ligand with its 2-D drawing, and the live summary](assets/ui/input-builder.png) | ![Run panel with phase tracker, timer and log, while running and after a failure](assets/ui/run-panel.png) | | **Result card** | **Run settings** | | ![Result card with confidence scores and the binding-affinity summary](assets/ui/result-card.png) | ![Quality presets and run settings](assets/ui/run-settings.png) | - **A guided form** that checks your input as you type: sequences, chain IDs, SMILES (with a 2-D drawing) and CCD codes, with a live summary and YAML preview. - **Confidence scores** that are easy to read: per-residue pLDDT, the predicted aligned error (PAE) with chain-to-chain blocks, ipTM and interface summaries. - **Binding affinity** for small-molecule ligands: the probability that the ligand binds, and the predicted IC50 in µM and nM, with pIC50 and an approximate ΔG. - **Several samples per job** if you want them, with the spread across samples reported. - **A self-contained HTML report** for each job: figures, the 3-D structure, tables and everything needed to reproduce the run. - **Clear failures:** when a run fails, the notebook names the likely cause and how to fix it. - **Light and dark themes**, and a layout that works on screens from 360 px wide. ## Reading the results | Quantity | What it means | |:--|:--| | **pLDDT** (0 to 100) | Confidence per residue: above 90 very high, 70 to 90 high, 50 to 70 low, below 50 very low. Ligands and modified residues get one value per heavy atom. | | **PAE** (Å) | Expected position error between two residues. It is asymmetric (row: aligned residue, column: scored residue); blocks between two chains show how confident the interface is. | | **Confidence score, pTM, ipTM** | Boltz's ranking metrics. Sample 0 is the best-ranked sample. | | **Binding probability** | How likely the ligand is a binder. Use it to separate binders from decoys. | | **Predicted affinity** | log10 of the IC50 in µM: −2 is about 10 nM, 0 is 1 µM, 1 is 10 µM. Use it to rank close analogues, not to compare unrelated compounds. Meaningful for small molecules only. | ## Requirements - A Google account and a **GPU runtime** in Colab (T4 or better; use an L4 or A100 for large complexes). - About **6 GB** of model files are downloaded once per session. - The notebook installs the engine for you: `boltz 2.2.1` on Python 3.10 to 3.12, and the `boltz-community 2.10.12` fork on Python 3.13 runtimes, where the official package is not available yet. - Protein sequences are sent to the ColabFold MSA server to build alignments, unless you upload your own MSA or choose single-sequence mode. ## Troubleshooting | Problem | What to do | |:--|:--| | **CUDA out of memory** | Lower *Max MSA sequences* (for example 256), use 1 sample, or switch to an L4 or A100 runtime. | | **MSA server failed or timed out** | Try again later, upload an `.a3m` file, or choose single-sequence mode. | | **Invalid SMILES or unknown CCD code** | The form checks both while you type; fix the entry it marks. | | **A template cannot be read** | Use the template's `.cif` file, or a `.pdb` file with SEQRES records (files written by Boltz itself have none). The form warns about this when you upload. | | **Low pLDDT everywhere** | Often a disordered region or single-sequence mode: provide an MSA or a template. | Every failed run shows a likely cause and a fix. For an analysis that does not line up with the predicted files, run `python -m boltz2nb.doctor /content/boltz_data/` and include its output in an [issue](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/issues). ## Privacy Your inputs stay in your Colab runtime, except for the MSA request (your protein sequences go to the ColabFold server), the check of CCD codes with the PDB, and usage reports, which help improve the tool and contain no personal data. Usage reports are on by default: untick `SEND_USAGE_STATS` in the first cell to turn them off. See [PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md) for details. ## Run it on your own machine
Install and run without Colab ```bash git clone https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook && cd boltz2-notebook pip install -e ".[ligand,viewer]" "boltz[cuda]==2.2.1" export BOLTZ2NB_BASE_DIR=$PWD/boltz_data # where params.yaml, run_params.txt and the results live python - <<'PY' from boltz2nb.yaml_builder import build_yaml, write_yaml, simple_spec from boltz2nb.run_params import serialize_run_params, DEFAULTS write_yaml(build_yaml(simple_spec("MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQLEERLGL", ligand_smiles="CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", affinity=True)), "boltz_data/params.yaml") open("boltz_data/run_params.txt", "w").write(serialize_run_params(dict(DEFAULTS, job_name="demo"))) PY python scripts/common/Boltz_Run.py && python scripts/common/analysis.py # the report is written to boltz_data/demo/analysis/ ```
Run settings and their defaults | Setting | Default | Range | Meaning | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | Recycling steps | 3 | 1 to 20 | Refinement passes of the trunk | | Sampling steps | 200 | 10 to 1000 | Diffusion steps per sample | | Diffusion samples | 1 | 1 to 25 | Structures per job; 3 or more give a spread estimate | | Step scale | 1.638 | 0.5 to 5 | Lower values give more diverse samples | | Max MSA sequences | 8192 | 1 to 16384 | Depth cap of the alignment | | Subsample MSA | on, 1024 | | Faster and lighter on memory | | MSA pairing | greedy | greedy, complete | How chains of a complex are paired | | Steering potentials | off | | Physics-based potentials during sampling | The **Fast** preset uses 2 recycling steps, 50 sampling steps and an MSA depth of 256; **Scientific** uses 5 recycling steps, 5 samples and the steering potentials.
How it works The notebooks are thin shells. Cell 1 clones a pinned release tag of this repository and installs the `boltz2nb` package and the Boltz engine; the other cells run three scripts that call into the package: | Cell | Script | What it does | |:--|:--|:--| | Generate Parameters | `scripts/v1` or `scripts/v2/param_gen.py` | The input builder; writes `params.yaml` and `run_params.txt` | | Run Boltz2 Engine | `scripts/common/Boltz_Run.py` | Builds the `boltz predict` command, shows live progress and the result card; never overwrites an existing job folder | | Analyse Results | `scripts/common/analysis.py` | Maps confidence values to residues, computes interface and ensemble statistics, writes `analysis/_report.html` and `summary.json` | Each job folder also keeps `boltz.log`, `status.json` and `run_context.json` (engine, PyTorch and CUDA versions, GPU, the exact command and the input). The package, its tests and the release process are described in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
## Documentation - [Use cases](https://atharvatilewale.github.io/boltz2-notebook/docs/use-cases.html) and [FAQ](https://atharvatilewale.github.io/boltz2-notebook/docs/faq.html) on the website - [Batch guide](batch/README.md): high-throughput screens from CSV or FASTA - [Changelog](releases/CHANGELOG.md) and [version table](releases/version_table.md) - [Privacy](docs/PRIVACY.md) and, for maintainers, [receiving usage reports](docs/TELEMETRY.md) - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [verification log](docs/VERIFICATION.md) ## Citation If Boltz2-Notebook helps your work, please cite the preprint, and Boltz-2 for the model: ```bibtex @article{Tilewale2026.09.18.752645, author = {Tilewale, Atharva and Patel, Dhaval}, title = {Boltz2-Notebook: An Interactive Google Colab Platform for Diffusion-Based Biomolecular Structure and Binding Affinity Prediction using the Boltz2 model}, journal = {bioRxiv}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.64898/2026.09.18.752645}, url = {https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2026/09/24/2026.09.18.752645}, publisher = {Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory} } @article{Passaro2025, author = {Passaro, Saro and Corso, Gabriele and Wohlwend, Jeremy and others}, title = {Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction}, journal = {bioRxiv}, year = {2025}, doi = {10.1101/2025.06.14.659707} } @article{Wohlwend2024, author = {Wohlwend, Jeremy and Corso, Gabriele and Passaro, Saro and others}, title = {Boltz-1: Democratizing Biomolecular Interaction Modeling}, journal = {bioRxiv}, year = {2024}, doi = {10.1101/2024.11.19.624167} } ``` ## Authors and acknowledgements Developed by [Atharva Tilewale](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale) and Dr. Dhaval Patel at Gujarat Biotechnology University. Built on [Boltz](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz) by Wohlwend, Corso, Passaro and colleagues, and on [boltz-community](https://github.com/Novel-Therapeutics/boltz-community) for Python 3.13 runtimes. Alignments come from the [ColabFold](https://github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold) MSA server. Questions and ideas are welcome in [Discussions](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/discussions); bugs go to [Issues](https://github.com/AtharvaTilewale/boltz2-notebook/issues). one_liner: Zephyr 是用扩散模型+GNN 从 MD 轨迹采样无序蛋白构象集合的生成工具，面向 IDP 结构建模但聚焦单链构象采样，未涉及无序分子互作/结合界面预测。
card:
## 是什么

Zephyr 是一个基于生成扩散模型的框架，用于对无序蛋白（IDP）的构象进行采样。它通过两个级联的图神经网络（GNN）实现：一个用于生成粗粒化（CG）结构（每个残基一个主链珠和一个侧链珠），另一个用于在给定粗粒化结构的情况下生成重原子坐标。模型在单个蛋白序列的分子动力学（MD）轨迹上训练，旨在生成与训练数据分布一致的结构系综。

## 亮点

- **两阶段生成架构**：将粗粒化采样与原子级细化分离，降低生成高维原子坐标的难度，同时保持化学合理性。
- **基于 MD 数据的训练**：直接利用 MD 轨迹作为训练数据，使模型学习到物理上合理的构象分布，而非仅依赖经验势函数。
- **灵活的配置系统**：使用 Python 文件作为配置，支持复杂逻辑和模块导入，便于实验定制和复现。
- **数据与权重托管**：数据集和模型权重存储在 Zenodo 上，支持按需下载，便于可重复性。
- **丰富的分析工具**：提供 `analysis` 模块用于比较数据集属性，以及 `figures` 模块用于复现论文图表。

## 为何对本课题有用

Zephyr 直接针对 IDR/IDP 的构象系综采样问题，是扩散模型在无序蛋白领域的典型应用。对于本课题（IDR/IDP × 分子互作 × 计算与 AI），其价值在于：
- **构象系综生成**：提供了一种可训练的生成模型，能够从 MD 数据中学习并生成无序蛋白的构象系综，可作为分子模拟的替代或补充。
- **互作建模基础**：生成的构象可作为下游分子对接或互作分析的输入，为研究无序蛋白在相分离中的互作模式提供结构基础。
- **方法学迁移**：其两阶段生成策略（粗粒化到原子）可迁移到其他生物分子系统，如 RNA 或蛋白复合物的构象采样。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：训练脚本为 `train.py`，采样脚本为 `models/generate.py`（通过 `python -m models.generate` 调用）。
- **安装**：使用 `pip install -r requirements.txt` 或 `conda env create -f requirements.yml`（Python 3.11）。若需 GPU 训练，需重新安装 PyTorch 的 CUDA 版本。
- **配置**：在 `configs/` 目录下创建或修改配置文件（如 `config_CS1.py`、`config_HA1.py`），可通过命令行参数覆盖配置值。
- **数据**：数据集（MD、处理后的、生成的）从 Zenodo 下载，通过 `data/datasets.py` 中的 `load_dataset(name)` 加载。输入格式为 MD 轨迹（如 DCD/PDB），输出为生成的 PDB 结构。
- **GPU 需求**：训练和采样需要 GPU 加速（PyTorch CUDA），但 CPU 也可运行（速度较慢）。
- **调试示例**：`analysis/analysis_tutorial.py` 提供了分析示例；`run_all.sh` 总结了论文中的训练和采样命令，可用于断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于**两阶段扩散生成**：先通过 GNN 生成粗粒化结构（降低维度），再以粗粒化结构为条件生成原子级结构，从而在保持计算效率的同时捕捉无序蛋白的构象多样性。这种分层生成策略有效解决了高维原子坐标生成的困难，并利用了 MD 数据的物理先验。

## 可搬移点

- **扩散模型实现**：`models/diffusers.py` 和 `models/noise_schedules.py` 中的扩散过程与噪声调度逻辑，可解耦后用于其他构象生成任务。
- **GNN 层与特征**：`models/layers.py` 和 `models/features.py` 中的图神经网络层和特征提取模块，可移植到自定义的蛋白表示学习 Pipeline。
- **损失函数**：`models/losses.py` 中的损失函数设计（可能包含物理约束），可借鉴用于训练其他生成模型。
- **数据加载与处理**：`data/process.py` 和 `data/datasets.py` 中的 MD 轨迹处理逻辑，可复用于其他 MD 数据集的预处理。
- **License**：MIT License，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体条款（如署名要求）。
readme: # Zephyr A generative diffusion model for sampling disordered protein structures trained on MD datasets. ## Introduction This codebase provides workflows to train a generative graph neural network (GNN) for the task of sampling conformations of disordered proteins. The generative model consists of 2 separate networks: 1) A GNN to sample coarse-grained protein structures and 2) another GNN to sample heavy atom positions with a given coarse-grained structure. The coarse-grained structure consists of a backbone bead (centered on the alpha-carbon atom) and a sidechain bead for each residue in the sequence. The models are trained on structures from molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Each model is trained on MD trajectories of a single protein sequence. ## Installation ### Option 1: Install packages with pip 1. Open a terminal and navigate to the root directory of this repository. 2. Create a virtual environment using `python=3.11`. 3. Install required packages with pip: ``` pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### Option 2: Install environment with conda Create a conda environment using the `.yml` file: ``` conda env create -f requirements.yml ``` If training with cuda device is required, reinstall pytorch with gpu support: ``` conda install -c nvidia -c pytorch pytorch pytorch-cuda torchvision --force-reinstall ``` ## Configs `config.py` holds variables that define global configurations. The default values can be overwritten by modifying the config variables in `config.py` or by defining a `config_defaults.py` located in the `configs` subdirectory. Configuration values for training and sampling with specific models must be stored in the `./configs` directory. Since configurations are `.py` files, one can import modules and use complex logic to define the configuration variables. However, at the end of the config file, one must delete all temporary variables to make sure that the module namespace contains only variables that are defined as configuration. Four configuration files are included in the repository: * `config_CS1.py`: configuration of the coarse-structure model * `config_CS1_NoCP.py`: configuration of the coarse-structure model that doesn't have cross-product modules. * `config_HA1.py`: configuration of the fine-structure model * `config_HA1_NoCP.py`: configuration of the fine-structure model that doesn't have cross-product modules. These configuration files were used to train models and sample datasets analyzed in the associated publication. To train without wandb logging, set `wandb = False` in your config file. ## Datasets Three kinds of datasets are associated with the codebase: MD, processed and generated datasets. The datasets are stored on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/23177444). Functions in `data.download` download a dataset as it is needed. Alternatively, one can download the dataset `.zip` files and extract them in a given directory. The config variables `MD_datasets_dir`, `proc_datasets_dir` and `gen_datasets_dir` specify the directories where the MD, processed and generated datasets are stored, respectively. Once datasets are downloaded, use the function `load_dataset(name)` in `data/datasets.py` to load a dataset named `name`. The name of a dataset matches the name of its directory. For example, `load_dataset('nup98_12')` will load data from the processed dataset directory `nup98_12` located in the directory defined by `config.proc_datasets_dir`. ## Weights Model weights are stored on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/23177444) in the `model_weights.zip` file. When specific model weights are needed for retraining or sampling, they are fetched from the Zenodo repository. Alternatively, one can download all model weights and store them in the directory defined by `config.weights_dir`. ## Training Model training is achieved by calling `train.py` with a given set of configurations. For example, ``` python train.py --configs my_config.py ``` will train a model using configurations defined in `my_config.py`. Configuration values can also be overwritten when calling `train.py`: ``` python train.py --configs my_config.py --batch_size 32 --N_workers 2 ``` will use a batch size of 32 and 2 workers, regardless of the values defined in `my_config.py`. One can also change the dataset used to train the model and its particular set of `train/valid/test` splits as follows: ``` python train.py --configs config_CS1.py --dataset nup98_12 --dataset_split_set_ID 1 ``` See `run_all.sh` for a summary of all training runs associated with the publication. ## Sampling Sampling with a given model is carried out with the `models.generate` module. For example, ``` python -m models.generate --ID_coarse C1 --ID_fine H1 --dataset nup98_12 --configs_coarse config_CS1.py --configs_fine config_HA1.py ``` will generate structures with the same topology as the `nup98_12` dataset using `config_CS1.py` for the coarse-structure model configurations and `config_HA1.py` for the fine-structure model configurations. The ID of the coarse-structure sampling is `C1` and the ID of the fine-structure sampling is `H1`. The dataset of generated structures will be stored in the directory defined by `config.gen_datasets_dir`. See `run_all.sh` for a summary of all sampling runs associated with the publication. ### Denoising Trajectories Examples of denoising trajectories for sampling the coarse structure and fine structure of the `nup98_12` sequence are shown. ## Analysis See `./analysis/analysis_tutorial.py` for an example of various ways to compare properties between datasets. ## Figures Modules in the `figures` directory contain plotting functions to recreate the figures of the associated publication. ## License This project is licensed under the MIT License — see the license file for details. ## References Olivier Trottier, Jack H. Gwozdecky and Sarah Rauscher (2026) "Generating Structural Ensembles of Disordered Proteins with Diffusion Models" [bioRxiv](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.10.02.756250v1).

## 是什么

这是一个面向 **MUC2 黏蛋白长 PTS 结构域**（Pro-Thr-Ser 串联重复、属于典型的 **IDR/IDP**）的**开源全原子 MD 分析流水线**，由 Northeastern University 的 Joshua Mantey 发布。仓库本身不含模拟引擎，而是以 **Jupyter Notebook 集合**的形式，对三套不同 O-糖基化程度（非糖基化 / 中度糖基化 / 高度糖基化）的 AMBER 轨迹（合计约 10,800 ns，每系统 3×1200 ns、2381 帧、1.2 ns/帧、TIP3P 显式溶剂）做系统化后处理，回答两个问题：(1) MUC2 PTS 骨架的固有生物物理与高分子性质；(2) O-糖基化与配体互作如何逐步重塑这些性质。

## 亮点

- **端到端可复现的分析分层**：把分析明确拆成 Stage 1（局部几何 / 全局高分子力学 / 构象采样）与 Stage 2（关联运动 / 互作网络 / 热力学），每个子主题对应一个独立 notebook，职责单一、便于局部替换。
- **多系统对照设计**：三套糖基化状态 × 3 条独立轨迹，天然支持收敛性检查（如 `pca_last400_comparison.ipynb` 只取最后 400 ns 做 PCA 对比）。
- **方法学细节到位**：包含 cross-normalised DCCM（把“关联模式变化”与“涨落幅度变化”解耦）、WLC 拟合求 persistence length、滑窗 Lp、PMF 的 reference 与 corrected 两套公式对照、DSSP 逐帧二级结构统计。
- **工程轻量**：纯 Python + MDAnalysis + numpy/scipy/matplotlib/pandas，无自建框架，notebook 可交互也可用 `nbconvert` 非交互批量执行（`run_physical_vars.sh` 即为此类脚本）。
- **MIT 许可**：可自由使用、修改、分发（需署名）。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库与课题 **IDR/IDP × 分子互作 × 物理模拟** 高度同向，属于“无序区构象系综 + 糖基化修饰 + 互作建模”的实证范例：

- **IDR 构象系综刻画**：PTS 域是串联重复 IDR，仓库给出了一套可直接迁移的系综分析组合拳——Cα 曲率/弯曲角、φ/ψ 二面角分布、DSSP（PPII/coil 含量）、PCA + 自由能面（FES）、PMF。这些正是 IDP 系综表征的标准量。
- **翻译后修饰（O-Glycan）对无序链力学的影响**：直接量化“糖基化如何把柔性无序肽变成刚性棒状纤维”，对理解 **mucin 类 IDR 的 LLPS/凝胶化** 提供物理机制证据（弯曲重分布、双峰角分布 → 宏观黏弹性）。
- **互作建模线索**：`hbond_analysis.ipynb` 分析链内与链–溶剂氢键占据率、骨架供体/受体可及性，直接关联“配体结合能力”；DCCM 显示糖基化增强长程关联，意味着配体结合效应可沿链传播更远——这是 IDR 变构/多价互作建模的可迁移观察。
- **可迁移到无序蛋白语言模型/采样**：其 PCA/FES/PMF 与 DCCM 流程可作为生成式模型（如 IDP 语言模型、扩散采样）输出系综的**下游评估器**，用于检验生成构象的力学与关联统计是否与 MD 一致。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：无单一 CLI 入口，入口即各 `*.ipynb`。按 README 的 Stage 1 / Stage 2 顺序阅读执行；批量执行可用 `run_physical_vars.sh` 或 `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace <notebook>.ipynb`。
- **安装与依赖**：`conda create -n muc2_analysis python=3.10`，然后 `pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pandas jupyter mdanalysis`（README 未提供 `requirements.txt`/`environment.yml`，依赖以 README 命令为准）。
- **数据路径**：每个 notebook 顶部有 `BASE` 变量，需改为本地数据目录。
- **输入格式**：AMBER 拓扑 `.prmtop`、对齐后的轨迹 `.xtc`（每系统 3 条独立 run），以及预计算的曲率/PCA/物理变量数据文件（`.dat`、`.csv`）。
- **输出**：以图与统计量为主（弯曲角分布、Rg/ETE、Lp、RMSF、DCCM 矩阵、FES/PMF 曲线、DSSP 占比等），README 未说明是否导出结构化结果文件。
- **GPU**：README 未说明需要 GPU；分析为 CPU 后处理。
- **Demo/单测**：仓库内**无单元测试**；notebook 本身即示例，但**轨迹与原始数据未随仓库提供**（因体积），需联系作者获取，因此开箱即跑不可行，只能作为方法模板断点调试。

## 核心 idea

把“糖基化对无序链的力学改造”从**全局刚度**问题重新表述为**弯曲的空间重分布 + 双峰构象切换**问题：总弯曲量近似守恒，但糖基化把部分残基推向更伸展、部分推向更弯折，并把 pre-glycan 位点的单峰角分布劈成双峰——即骨架在两个能量极小间切换，从而在宏观上解释黏液凝胶的黏弹性。方法学上，用 **cross-normalised DCCM** 把“关联模式变化”从“涨落幅度变化”中剥离，是让“糖基化增强长程关联”这一结论站得住脚的关键技巧。

## 可搬移点

- **`radius_of_curvature.ipynb` 的 Cα 内部虚拟键角曲率计算 + pre-glycan hotspot 识别**：可直接解耦为函数，用于任意 IDR 的逐残基弯曲谱与修饰位点预判。
- **`persistence_length.ipynb` 的 WLC 拟合 + 滑窗 Lp**：标准高分子力学量，可移植到任何 IDR/IDP 系综的刚度评估。
- **`dccm_crossnorm.ipynb` 的 cross-normalised DCCM**：最值得拷贝的“去幅度化”关联分析模块，用于比较不同修饰/突变/配体条件下的关联模式。
- **`pmf_ref_formula.ipynb` / `pmf_corrected_formula.ipynb` 的 PMF 双公式对照**：可作为沿 PC1/PC2 构建自由能面的参考实现，用于系综重加权与构象稳定性比较。
- **`hbond_analysis.ipynb` 的氢键占据率 + 骨架可及性统计**：可迁移为 IDR–配体互作建模的特征提取层。
- **`pca_last400_comparison.ipynb` 的收敛性检查范式**：可复用于任何 MD/生成系综的采样充分性验证。
- **License**：MIT，允许拷贝、修改、再分发（需保留署名与许可声明）。注意：**代码可搬移，但轨迹数据未随仓库发布**，复用前需自行准备或联系作者获取数据。

# MUC2 Glycosylation Analysis
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/) [![Jupyter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter-Notebooks-F37626?logo=jupyter&logoColor=white)](https://jupyter.org/) [![Open Source](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20Source-%E2%9D%A4-red.svg)](https://github.com/jkamantey/muc2-glycosylation-analysis) [![AMBER](https://img.shields.io/badge/Force%20Field-AMBER-green.svg)]() **Open-source MD analysis pipeline for the MUC2 mucin long PTS domain** *How O-glycosylation reshapes backbone mechanics, polymer properties, and ligand interaction capacity*
--- ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#overview) - [Systems](#systems) - [Analysis Pipeline](#analysis-pipeline) - [Notebooks](#notebooks) - [Key Findings](#key-findings) - [Installation](#installation) - [Data](#data) - [Citation](#citation) - [License](#license) - [Author](#author) --- ## Overview **MUC2** is the dominant gel-forming glycoprotein of the intestinal mucus layer. Its **long PTS (Pro-Thr-Ser) domain** — a tandem-repeat intrinsically disordered region carrying up to 30 O-linked glycan chains — is responsible for the mucus gel's unique mechanical properties: rigidity, hydration, and selective permeability. This repository provides a complete, reproducible computational pipeline that answers two connected questions: > **1.** What are the intrinsic biophysical and polymer properties of the MUC2 PTS backbone? > > **2.** How do O-glycosylation and ligand interactions progressively reshape those properties? The pipeline moves from local backbone geometry (per-residue bending, dihedral angles) through global chain mechanics (persistence length, radius of gyration) to correlated dynamics and free energy landscapes — building a full structural picture of how glycosylation transforms a flexible disordered peptide into a stiff, rod-like mucin fibre. --- ## Systems Three glycosylation states are compared across **~10,800 ns** of all-atom MD simulation: | System | Description | Colour | Simulation | |--------|-------------|--------|------------| | **Non-glycosylated** | Naked PTS backbone, no O-glycans | ![#A23B72](https://placehold.co/12x12/A23B72/A23B72.png) `#A23B72` | 3 × 1200 ns | | **Mid-level Glycosylated** | Partial O-glycosylation | ![#2E86AB](https://placehold.co/12x12/2E86AB/2E86AB.png) `#2E86AB` | 3 × 1200 ns | | **Ext. Glycosylated** | Full / dense O-glycosylation | ![#F18F01](https://placehold.co/12x12/F18F01/F18F01.png) `#F18F01` | 3 × 1200 ns | > 2381 frames per system · 1.2 ns/frame · AMBER force field · explicit solvent (TIP3P) --- ## Analysis Pipeline ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ STAGE 1 — Biophysical │ │ Characterise the MUC2 backbone │ ├──────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤ │ Local geometry │ Global polymer │ Conformational sampling │ │ │ mechanics │ │ │ · Cα curvature │ · Rg, ETE │ · PCA (PC1, PC2) │ │ · Pre-glycan │ · Persistence │ · Free energy surface │ │ bending │ length │ · Dihedral distributions │ │ · φ/ψ angles │ · RMSF │ · Secondary structure │ │ · Twist profile │ │ │ └──────────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ STAGE 2 — Dynamics & Interactions │ │ How glycosylation reshapes properties & binding │ ├──────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤ │ Correlated │ Interaction │ Thermodynamics │ │ motions │ network │ │ │ │ │ │ │ · DCCM │ · H-bond │ · PMF / FES │ │ · Cross-norm │ occupancy │ · Conformational │ │ DCCM │ · Ligand │ barriers │ │ │ accessibility │ │ └──────────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ## Notebooks ### Stage 1 — Biophysical Properties | Notebook | Description | |----------|-------------| | [`radius_of_curvature.ipynb`](radius_of_curvature.ipynb) | Cα interior virtual bond-angle curvature · per-residue bending profiles · pre-glycan structural hotspot analysis · bimodal distribution characterisation | | [`rmsf_comparison.ipynb`](rmsf_comparison.ipynb) | Per-residue RMSF across all three systems · identifies stiffened and mobilised regions | | [`plot_physical_vars.ipynb`](plot_physical_vars.ipynb) | PCA coloured by Rg · ETE · curvature · persistence length · free energy surface · Pearson correlations with PC axes | | [`persistence_length.ipynb`](persistence_length.ipynb) | Worm-like chain (WLC) fit · sliding-window Lp · stiffness comparison across glycosylation states | | [`phi_psi_bend_analysis.ipynb`](phi_psi_bend_analysis.ipynb) | Ramachandran scatter from mean structures · bend redistribution profiles · Cα dihedral twist analysis | | [`dihedral_distribution.ipynb`](dihedral_distribution.ipynb) | Backbone φ/ψ dihedral distributions · conformational basin populations | | [`secondary_structure.ipynb`](secondary_structure.ipynb) | DSSP secondary structure per residue per frame · PPII / coil content vs glycosylation | ### Stage 2 — Dynamics, Correlations & Interactions | Notebook | Description | |----------|-------------| | [`dccm_glyc_noglyc.ipynb`](dccm_glyc_noglyc.ipynb) | Dynamic cross-correlation matrix (DCCM) · glyc vs non-glyc | | [`dccm_comparison.ipynb`](dccm_comparison.ipynb) | DCCM comparison across all three glycosylation states | | [`dccm_crossnorm.ipynb`](dccm_crossnorm.ipynb) | Cross-normalised DCCM · isolates changes in correlation pattern independent of fluctuation magnitude | | [`hbond_analysis.ipynb`](hbond_analysis.ipynb) | Intra-chain and chain–solvent H-bond occupancy · backbone donor/acceptor accessibility for ligand binding | | [`pmf_ref_formula.ipynb`](pmf_ref_formula.ipynb) | Potential of mean force (PMF) along PC1/PC2 · reference formula | | [`pmf_corrected_formula.ipynb`](pmf_corrected_formula.ipynb) | PMF · corrected formula · conformational stability comparison | ### PCA & Conformational Sampling | Notebook | Description | |----------|-------------| | [`muc2_newsystem.ipynb`](muc2_newsystem.ipynb) | Combined PCA · glycosylated + non-glycosylated · shared conformational space | | [`muc2_noglycans.ipynb`](muc2_noglycans.ipynb) | PCA · non-glycosylated system only | | [`pca_dccm_noglyc_domains.ipynb`](pca_dccm_noglyc_domains.ipynb) | PCA + DCCM by domain · non-glycosylated | | [`pca_dccm_normal_domains.ipynb`](pca_dccm_normal_domains.ipynb) | PCA + DCCM by domain · glycosylated | | [`pca_last400_comparison.ipynb`](pca_last400_comparison.ipynb) | PCA of last 400 ns per run · convergence check | --- ## Key Findings
1. The sequence pre-encodes structural hotspots at glycan sites 25 out of 30 pre-glycan positions already form a local bending peak in the **non-glycosylated** chain — before any glycan is attached. The backbone geometry is shaped by the amino acid sequence to anticipate glycosylation. The 5 non-rising sites are all **Glycine**, falling at exactly position 6 of every 6-residue tandem repeat unit.
2. Glycine acts as the periodic conformational hinge Glycine is the only amino acid with no side chain, giving it exceptional conformational freedom. It cannot hold the backbone in the extended geometry that Thr, Ile, Val, and Pro enforce — instead it dips into a more kinked state. This makes it the structurally weakest point in each repeat unit, and the site of the **largest glycan-driven conformational rescue** (up to +15.6° at a single Gly site under full glycosylation).
3. Glycosylation redistributes bending rather than uniformly stiffening The total summed bending across the chain is similar between systems, but its spatial distribution changes: some residues become more extended while others become more kinked. This redistribution — not simple global stiffening — is the dominant mechanical effect of glycosylation.
4. Bimodal angle distributions signal conformational switching Rather than shifting all pre-glycan residues to a new single preferred angle, glycosylation splits the population into two distinct peaks. The backbone switches between two energy minima — a behaviour that at the macroscopic scale underpins the viscoelastic (simultaneously solid-like and liquid-like) mechanics of mucus gels.
5. Long-range correlated motions increase with glycosylation DCCM analysis shows that glycosylation introduces longer-range dynamic correlations along the chain. This has direct consequences for ligand interactions: a ligand binding at one region can propagate its structural effect further along the chain in the glycosylated system than in the naked backbone.
--- ## Key Results Table | Property | Non-glycosylated | Mid-glycosylated | Ext. glycosylated | |----------|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Mean Cα bend angle (°) | ~116–120 | ~119–124 | ~122–128 | | Gly-site Δ angle from non-glyc (°) | — | up to +10 | up to **+16** | | Pre-glycan angle distribution | unimodal · narrow | bimodal · broader | bimodal · broad | | Bend redistribution | baseline | partial | strong | | Chain stiffness (Lp) | lowest | intermediate | highest | | Long-range DCCM correlations | weakest | intermediate | strongest | --- ## Installation ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/jkamantey/muc2-glycosylation-analysis.git cd muc2-glycosylation-analysis # Create a conda environment conda create -n muc2_analysis python=3.10 conda activate muc2_analysis # Install dependencies pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pandas jupyter mdanalysis ``` ### Running a notebook interactively ```bash jupyter notebook ``` ### Running a notebook non-interactively ```bash jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute \ --ExecutePreprocessor.kernel_name=anaconda-base \ --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=600 \ --inplace .ipynb ``` ### Setting your data path Each notebook has a `BASE` variable near the top pointing to the local data directory. Update it to match your system before running: ```python BASE = '/path/to/your/data/' ``` --- ## Data Trajectory files (`.xtc`), topology files (`.prmtop`), and raw data arrays (`.dat`, `.csv`) are **not included** in this repository due to file size. The notebooks load data via relative paths from the `BASE` variable. To reproduce the analysis, you will need: - AMBER topology (`.prmtop`) for each system - Aligned trajectory files (`.xtc`) for each of the three independent runs - Pre-computed curvature, PCA, and physical variable data files Contact the author if you are interested in accessing the simulation data. --- ## Citation If you use this code or analysis pipeline in your work, please cite: ```bibtex @software{mantey2026muc2, author = {Mantey, Joshua}, title = {MUC2 Glycosylation Analysis: MD Simulation Pipeline}, year = {2026}, publisher = {GitHub}, url = {https://github.com/jkamantey/muc2-glycosylation-analysis}, institution = {Northeastern University} } ``` --- ## License This project is licensed under the **MIT License** — free to use, modify, and distribute with attribution. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for full details. --- ## Author **Joshua Mantey** Northeastern University [mantey.j@northeastern.edu](mailto:mantey.j@northeastern.edu) *Computational biophysics · MUC2 mucin glycobiology · Intrinsically disordered proteins · Molecular dynamics*

## 是什么
IFF 是一个基于机器学习的工具，用于识别蛋白质固有无序区域（IDR）中的关键残基。它通过训练模型来预测哪些残基在无序区域中具有功能重要性，并提供注意力图可视化以辅助解释。

## 亮点
- 提供完整的 Jupyter Notebook 工作流，从数据准备到模型训练再到特征可视化，便于复现和调试。
- 支持通过 Binder 在线运行注意力图可视化，降低使用门槛。
- 依赖管理清晰，使用 pyproject.toml 固定版本，并包含 Dockerfile 便于环境复现。
- 集成多种生物信息学工具（如 Biopython、OMAdb）和机器学习库（PyTorch、scikit-learn），功能全面。

## 为何对本课题有用
该仓库直接针对 IDR 关键残基识别，与课题方向高度相关。其方法可迁移至无序蛋白互作位点预测、相分离驱动残基识别等任务。注意力图可视化技术可帮助理解模型关注的序列特征，为无序蛋白语言模型提供可解释性参考。此外，其数据准备流程（从 OMA 获取序列、PONDR 标注）可复用于构建 IDR 相关数据集。

## 怎么用
- 主入口：Jupyter Notebook 文件（如 `2_model_training.ipynb`、`3_trained_feature_vis.ipynb`），以及 `src/iff/__init__.py` 中的 `iff` 命令行入口。
- 安装：使用 `pyproject.toml` 中的依赖，通过 `pip install .` 或 `uv` 安装；也可使用 Dockerfile 构建镜像。
- 输入数据：FASTA 序列（来自 OMA 数据库）和 PONDR 预测结果（用于标注无序区域）。
- 输出：模型预测结果和注意力图（可视化）。
- 是否需要 GPU：依赖中指定 `torch==1.13.0+cpu`，CPU 即可运行，但 GPU 可加速训练。
- 调试示例：`feature_vis_on_binder.ipynb` 可直接在 Binder 上运行，适合断点调试。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学在于利用机器学习模型（可能基于注意力机制）学习 IDR 中残基的上下文特征，并通过注意力权重识别关键残基。其创新点在于将无序区域的功能位点预测转化为可解释的注意力图，从而提供生物学可解释的预测。

## 可搬移点
- 数据准备模块（`function/omaseq.py`、`function/cutpondr.py`、`function/seqfilter.py`）可解耦用于构建自定义 IDR 数据集。
- 注意力可视化代码（`function/dlcode/atten.py`）可移植到其他无序蛋白模型中用于可解释性分析。
- 模型训练流程（`2_model_training.ipynb`）可参考其数据加载和训练循环设计。
- License 未在资料中说明，需确认。

## 是什么

OpenPhase（仓库名 ConditionPhase）是一个面向生物分子液-液相分离（LLPS）的开源平台与数据集，提供条件感知（condition-aware）的系统级探索，将环境因素（盐浓度、温度、pH 等）纳入相行为建模。它包含三个数据集（db1: LLPSDBv2 处理数据；db2: 实验室记录；db3: RNAPSEC 数据），并定义了三个规范任务：相分离结果预测、条件推断、相系统设计（生成蛋白序列）。

## 亮点

- **条件感知建模**：超越纯序列预测，显式整合环境因子，这是 LLPS 领域少有的系统级视角。
- **多源数据整合**：涵盖蛋白、RNA、DNA 序列，以及体外/体内实验记录，数据规模大（P 空间 11,439 条记录 + 6,338 个正例蛋白；N+U 空间 35,107 个蛋白）。
- **标准化基准**：为三个任务提供统一的训练/测试划分、基线模型和评估指标，便于可复现研究。
- **交互式可视化网站**：浏览器端运行，支持明暗主题，便于探索数据。
- **模块化代码结构**：离散模型（Discrete/）与潜在扩散模型（ldm/）分离，便于扩展。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接针对 IDR/IDP 与 LLPS 的交叉领域，是课题的核心资源：
- **数据价值**：db1/db2/db3 提供了带相分离注释的序列和条件数据，可用于训练 IDR 相分离预测模型或验证构象系综假设。
- **任务对齐**：三个规范任务（结果预测、条件推断、序列设计）与课题中的互作建模、条件依赖的相行为预测高度契合。
- **方法迁移**：其条件感知框架可迁移到 IDP 构象系综采样中，将环境参数作为条件变量，改进生成模型的物理合理性。
- **生成模型**：ldm 中的潜在扩散模型（含 ESM-C 条件 U-Net）可用于设计具有目标相行为的多肽/蛋白序列，直接支持课题中的“无序蛋白语言模型”方向。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库根目录下的 `task1.py`、`task2.py`、`task3.py` 分别对应三个规范任务；`db1.py`、`db2.py`、`db3.py` 提供数据集接口。
- **安装**：`git clone https://github.com/nicetone9/ConditionPhase.git`，依赖见 `requirements.txt` 或 `setup.py`（README 未列出具体依赖）。
- **数据加载示例**：
  ```python
  from db1 import DB1Dataset
  from db2 import DB2Dataset
  from db3 import DB3Dataset
  db1 = DB1Dataset()
  db2 = DB2Dataset()
  db3 = DB3Dataset()
  ```
- **输入/输出格式**：序列数据（蛋白/RNA/DNA）与条件（pH、盐浓度等），输出为相分离标签或生成序列；具体格式 README 未详细说明。
- **GPU 需求**：涉及扩散模型训练，建议使用 GPU 加速（README 未明确要求）。
- **调试入口**：`records_space/colab/` 下有多个 Colab 脚本（如 `rs03_run.py`、`rs04_figs.py`），以及 `test_rslib.py` 可用于测试；`Discrete/training.py` 和 `ldm/training.py` 提供训练流程。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察：将相分离预测从“序列到标签”的静态映射，升级为“序列 + 环境条件 → 相行为”的条件生成/预测框架，并通过潜在扩散模型（LDM）实现序列的生成式设计，从而将环境因素作为可控变量，实现系统级的相图探索。

## 可搬移点

- **条件嵌入模块**：`meta_embed.py` 和 `meta_config.py` 中的条件编码逻辑，可解耦后用于自定义 Pipeline，将环境参数注入任意序列模型。
- **数据集接口**：`db1.py`、`db2.py`、`db3.py` 的数据加载与预处理逻辑，可直接复用或改造，用于整合自己的 LLPS 数据。
- **扩散模型组件**：`ldm/` 下的 U-Net 条件去噪模型（`unet_denoising_esmc.py`）和扩散调度器（`Scheduler.py`）可独立提取，用于 IDP 构象生成或序列设计。
- **评估协议**：`Discrete/evaluator.py` 中的评估逻辑可迁移到自定义基准测试。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

（注：所有内容均基于提供的 README 和目录树，未涉及的部分标注为“README 未说明”。）

# OpenPhase OpenPhase: Condition-Aware Exploration of Biomolecular Phase Separation OpenPhase is an open-source platform and dataset designed to accelerate knowledge discovery in Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation (LLPS). It is the first condition-aware platform for system-level exploration of how environmental factors influence biomolecular phase behavior. ## 🌐 Interactive site **[nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/)** is the home page of the OpenPhase data resources. Click a part of the system figures to open the explorer on that system; every page has a light / dark switch and runs entirely in the browser. | System | What it holds | Page | |---|---|---| | **P** | 11,439 single-protein experiment records in one map, plus 6,338 proteins that the tools list as positives but that have no record (hollow rings) | [records_space/](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/records_space/) | | **N + U** | 35,107 proteins: the training negatives of ten tools and PPMC against a Swiss-Prot reference sample. No positives, no conditions | [records_space/negatives/](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/records_space/negatives/) | Multi-protein systems (protein(2), protein(3), complexes) are shown on the home page but are not in the explorer yet. Details, data notes and licences: [`records_space/README.md`](records_space/README.md). ## 🚀 Key Features ### Condition-Aware Modeling Moves beyond simple sequence prediction to incorporate extrinsic environmental factors (salt concentration, temperature, pH, etc.) that critically influence phase separation behavior. ### Comprehensive Datasets - **db1**: Processed LLPSDBv2 data containing proteins, RNA, and DNA sequences with phase separation annotations - **db2**: Manually collected records from laboratory notebooks covering both in vitro and in vivo experiments - **db3**: Preprocessed RNAPSEC data focused on protein-RNA interaction systems and their phase behavior ### Standardized Benchmarking Formalized tasks and evaluation protocols for: - Outcome prediction - Condition inference - Protein design - Reproducible research in LLPS ## 🛠️ Canonical Tasks ### 1. Phase Outcome Prediction Predicting whether a system undergoes LLPS (y ∈ {0, 1}) given: - Components (x): protein/RNA sequences - Conditions (c): environmental factors (pH, salt, temperature, etc.) ### 2. Condition Inference Inferring the potential experimental conditions (c) that lead to a specific phase separation outcome, enabling rational experimental design. ### 3. Phase System Design Generating potential protein sequences (x) that exhibit desired phase behaviors under target conditions using generative models. ## 📂 Repository Structure ``` ConditionPhase/ ├── discrete/ # Discrete model architectures ├── ldm/ # Latent diffusion model components ├── db1.py # LLPSDBv2 dataset interface ├── db2.py # Laboratory notebook dataset ├── db3.py # RNAPSEC dataset interface ├── meta_config.py # Configuration utilities ├── meta_embed.py # Embedding generation └── params_all.yaml # Global hyperparameters ``` ## 🔧 Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/nicetone9/ConditionPhase.git cd ConditionPhase # Install dependencies (see requirements.txt or setup.py) ``` ## 📊 Getting Started Load and explore datasets: ```python from db1 import DB1Dataset from db2 import DB2Dataset from db3 import DB3Dataset # Load datasets db1 = DB1Dataset() db2 = DB2Dataset() db3 = DB3Dataset() ``` ## 📚 Tasks & Benchmarks Each canonical task includes: - Standardized train/test splits - Baseline models - Evaluation metrics - Documentation in `task1.py`, `task2.py`, `task3.py` ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please refer to contribution guidelines and open issues for ongoing research directions. ## 📖 Citation If you use ConditionPhase in your research, please cite the associated publication. ## 📧 Contact For questions, suggestions, or collaborations, visit the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nicetone9/ConditionPhase) and contact [email](peiran@cmu.edu).
